title: Event
description: What one node reports having just done. Guard passes are events too - a guard that only speaks when it fires is, on a quiet day, indistinguishable from a guard that never ran. The run trace is computed from this stream and never stored, which is why node_id is required and cannot be added to runs already recorded.

engagement_id.description: Nothing runs unscoped, so nothing is emitted unscoped either.

node_id.description: The architecture-graph node that emitted this. Required: the run trace is derived from it and cannot be reconstructed later.

step_id.description: The compiled plan step, when the emitter was executing one. Null for resource and static nodes.

type.description: Dotted and typed: skill.dispatched, guard.tieout.pass, hitl.item.queued, loop.repair.result.

payload.description: Event-specific detail. Deliberately untyped here: an event schema that has to change whenever a node learns to say something new is an event schema people route around.
payload.x-open-by-design: The only open object in the registry. An event schema that has to change whenever a node learns to say something new is an event schema people route around, and emission is fire-and-forget precisely so observability never becomes a new way for work to break. Nothing validates against payload and no figure may travel in it.

diagnostic_code.description: Set on any event a person has to act on. Stable code from the diagnostics registry, e.g. GUARD.TIEOUT_MISMATCH.
